Since the involved guarantees and counter-guarantees were denominated in USD, the interest rate for calculating losses should not exceed the USD loan interest rate for the same period, and the periods for overseas service and the hearing on jurisdictional objections should be deducted.

This Court holds that the independent guarantees involved were denominated in USD. Moumou A Branch's claim to convert the principal into RMB and calculate capital occupation interest using the domestic bank loan interest rate for the same period lacks factual and legal basis. Capital occupation losses should be calculated by reference to internationally prevailing USD interest rates for the same period. After consulting the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) in USD from 2014 to 2020 through the Bloomberg information system, and considering the specific circumstances of the case, such as the amount of the preservation, the duration of the preservation, and the degree of fault of Moumou Electric Power Construction, this Court determines that the capital occupation losses to be paid by Moumou Electric Power Construction shall be calculated on a principal of USD 94,361,217 at an annualized rate of 1% from November 14, 2014, to April 15, 2020.

II. Whether Moumou Property Insurance Company Should Bear Liability

Moumou A Branch claimed that Moumou Property Insurance Company, having provided a guarantee for Moumou Electric Power Construction's property preservation, should bear joint and several liability for compensation. In this case, on June 27, 2016, Moumou Property Insurance Company issued a guarantee letter to Shandong High Court, providing a guarantee for Moumou Electric Power Construction's property preservation application in Case No. (2014) Lu Min Si Chu Zi No. 6. If Moumou Electric Power Construction's application was erroneous, Moumou Property Insurance Company would compensate the respondent for losses suffered due to the preservation. Therefore, Moumou Property Insurance Company shall bear joint and several liability for the above compensation liability of Moumou Electric Power Construction. This claim of Moumou A Branch has factual and legal basis, and this Court supports it.

III. Whether Moumou B Branch and Moumou C Branch Should Bear Liability

Moumou A Branch claimed that Moumou B Branch and Moumou C Branch unreasonably delayed payment. They should have paid Moumou A Branch under the terms of the independent counter-guarantees before Shandong High Court issued the preservation ruling suspending payment. They had no right to refuse payment of the claimed amounts under the counter-guarantees to Moumou A Branch based on Shandong High Court's preservation ruling. This constituted joint tort with Moumou Electric Power Construction, and they should bear joint compensation liability with Moumou Electric Power Construction. In this case, regarding the claim of delayed payment, although Moumou A Branch submitted Decisions No. 343 and 344 (DOCDEX), the four defendants did not recognize the authenticity of those decisions. Considering the content, the decisions were made based on an application from one party and lacked objectivity and fairness. The first-instance court's refusal to adopt them was not improper. The counter-guarantees involved all stated that the Uniform Rules for Demand Guarantees (URDG 458) applied. However, URDG 458 does not define "reasonable time." Therefore, the period from November 3, 2014, when Moumou A Branch sent claim notices to Moumou B Branch and Moumou C Branch, to November 14, 2014, when Moumou B Branch and Moumou C Branch received the suspension ruling from Shandong High Court and suspended payment under the involved guarantees, did not exceed a reasonable time. Accordingly, Moumou B Branch and Moumou C Branch did not have subjective intent to delay payment. Moumou A Branch's claim that Moumou B Branch and Moumou C Branch delayed payment before the delivery of the guarantee suspension ruling lacks corresponding factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. After the delivery of the suspension ruling, Moumou B Branch and Moumou C Branch lawfully suspended payment under the involved counter-guarantees and did not commit any tortious act. After the effective judgment of this Court in Case No. 513 was rendered, Moumou B Branch and Moumou C Branch promptly fulfilled their payment obligations, and there was no fault or blameworthiness on their part. As for the claim of malicious collusion, Moumou A Branch also did not submit corresponding evidence. Therefore, this ground of appeal by Moumou A Branch lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, Moumou A Branch's appeal is partially well-founded and shall be supported. In accordance with Article 15 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Disputes over Independent Guarantees, Article 108 and Article 177, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2021) Lu Min Chu No. 36 of Shandong High People's Court;

2. China Moumou Group Shandong Electric Power Construction Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay to Moumou Bank Shanghai Branch capital occupation losses calculated on a principal of USD 94,361,217 at an annualized rate of 1% from November 14, 2014, to April 15, 2020. China Moumou Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Shandong Branch shall bear joint and several liability for compensation.

3. Reject the other claims of Moumou Bank Shanghai Branch.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
